**About 200 W of solar** will refill a 1,000 Wh power station in roughly a day and a half of average sun. For a full refill in one average day, plan on about **300 W**.

- **Quick rule:** divide watt-hours by 5. That gives about 200 W for a 1,000 Wh station, which refills it in about a day and a half ([Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/)).
- **The math:** capacity ÷ (peak sun hours × loss factor). With 4.5 peak sun hours and a 0.75 factor, 1,000 ÷ (4.5 × 0.75) ≈ 296 W ([Enough Watts](https://enoughwatts.com/guides/how-much-solar-to-recharge)). A 200 W panel makes about 630 Wh on an average day, so it nearly fills a 1,000 Wh unit in a day and a half ([Watt48](https://www.watt48.com/guides/solar-panel-charging-power-station)).
- **Sun matters a lot:** at 4 peak sun hours, a 1,000 Wh station needs about 340 W for a one-day refill ([Power Runtime](https://power-runtime.pages.dev/guides/solar-charging/)). In a northern winter, the same job can take 700 W or more ([Held in Reserve](https://www.heldinreserve.com/power/solar-panels-recharge-power-station/)).

**Check before buying:**
- **Solar input limit:** the station caps how many watts it accepts. Panels above that cap add nothing ([Enough Watts](https://enoughwatts.com/guides/how-much-solar-to-recharge)).
- **Voltage window:** a panel's open-circuit voltage must fit the station's input range, or the charge controller can be damaged ([Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/)).
